text: Title: Data Engineer | Agency: Central Intelligence Agency | Location: Washington, District of Columbia | Grade: GS-9 to 13. Summary: Data Engineers in the Directorate of Mission Systems (DMS) solve critical data challenges by building data pipelines, transforming data, and delivering data to systems to advance CIA's mission.

Title: Data Engineer | Agency: Central Intelligence Agency | Location: Washington, District of Columbia | Grade: GS-9 to 13. Duties: As a Directorate of Mission Systems (DMS) Data Engineer at CIA, you will transform and deliver high-priority datasets to enable exploitation and analysis for CIA's intelligence mission. Using computer programming and other capabilities, DMS Data Engineers develop processes to transform raw structured or unstructured data into useful, actionable information for critical mission systems. They design and build scalable data pipelines using commercial cloud, open source, and custom software solutions to process large datasets. DMS Data Engineers create automated data validation methods to load data into systems accurately and consistently. Through partnerships with collectors, data scientists, and software engineers, DMS Data Engineers design how data will be integrated and stored for optimal effectiveness. DMS Data Engineers are curious and use their skills to identify problems and build solutions, applying updated expertise in areas such as ETL, workflow and container orchestration, database and search technologies, distributed computing, serverless design, and cloud solutions. DMS encourages and supports continual learning. Opportunities exist for continued professional development, to include advanced technical training. Travel opportunities may be available.

Title: Information Technology Specialist (INFOSEC) | Agency: Department of the Air Force Headquarters | Location: Multiple Locations | Grade: GS-9 to 14. Duties: ****Duties and responsibilities vary and may increase according to grade level****. Utilize knowledge of IT principles, methods and security regulations and policies to carry out established base-wide policy to administer the INFOSEC (also known as COMPUSEC) program. Implement procedures to ensure protection of information transmitted to the installation, among organizations on the installation, and from the installation on the local or wide area networks, the world-wide-web, or other communications modes. Administer the Communications Security (COMSEC) program. Control and protect all cryptographic material and administer the Cryptographic Access Program (CAP). Conduct semi-annual functional reviews of all COMSEC user accounts, inspecting COMSEC facilities, reviewing procedures, and auditing all cryptographic holdings. Administer the COMPUSEC Program and protect Information Technology (IT) assets against unauthorized, accidental, or deliberate modification, disclosure, and destruction of data.

Title: IT SPEC (INFOSEC/NETWORK) - TITLE 32 | Agency: Air National Guard Units | Location: Hunter AFB, Georgia | Grade: GS-11. Duties: The following are the responsibilities of an IT Spec (Infosec/Network), GS-2210-11: Performs cyberspace operations that protect and defend (or assess the capability to protect and defend) information and information systems by ensuring their availability, integrity, authentication, confidentiality, and non-repudiation. Provides for mission assurance of information systems by incorporating protection, detection, and reaction capabilities. Conducts risk and vulnerability assessments of DoD information systems to identify associated vulnerabilities, risks and protection needs. Operates in-garrison and deployed cyberspace weapon systems. Performs activities such as configuring and monitoring hardware and software for systems operation, processing and control of data flow, and client-server multi-user system support, including network management or administration. Specializes in one or more of the following tasks. a. Evaluates and assesses vulnerabilities of customer network and application server hardware, operating systems, and peripheral network equipment such as routers, bridges, switches, attached cabling system, network interface cards, modems, multiplexers, and concentrators. Conducts evaluations to ensure compliance with applicable standards. Ensures system backups are performed to ensure expedient restoration of the database for the respective network equipment.

Title: IT SPEC (INFOSEC/NETWORK) - TITLE 32 | Agency: Air National Guard Units | Location: Hunter AFB, Georgia | Grade: GS-11. Duties: Evaluates effectiveness of customer network perimeter and internal defenses. b. Hunts for and illuminates advanced persistent threats in DOD Cyber systems and protects priority DOD missions for a specified duration. Detects, discovers and characterizes advanced adversary tradecraft. Monitors target systems/networks for unusual activity to identify and remove adversary activity that evade routine security measures on assigned cyber terrain. c. Performs analysis and design of automated and manual systems related to the network. Provides data for intrusion detection analysis. Determines applicability of established methods. Provides technical advice to users. Examines and evaluates alternative means of satisfying user requirements. Suggests technically feasible approaches and makes recommendations regarding the most effective countermeasures. d. Replicates tactics, techniques and procedures of specific cyber threats as appropriate to evaluate cyber defenses and prepare DOD defensive cyber operations. Assesses posture and processes from an outside perspective. Provides the ability to plan/conduct/enhance counter infiltration operations, mission protection operations, cyber readiness operations, cyber threat emulation operations and counter-measure development. e. Conducts cyber key terrain analysis and mission-oriented mapping, identifying cyber dependencies in mission owner network.

Title: IT SPEC (INFOSEC/NETWORK) - TITLE 32 | Agency: Air National Guard Units | Location: Hunter AFB, Georgia | Grade: GS-11. Duties: Develops courses of action for risk mitigation and mission defense and leads development of written plans which integrate team capabilities to provide these effects. f. Assesses and evaluates vulnerabilities and/or adversary activity in industrial control system (ICS) enclaves. Detects, characterizes, and resolves insecurities in ICS networks. Reviews and analyzes ICS network traffic, configurations, and operating procedures and provides recommendations to improve system security posture. Prepares Unit Training Assembly, Annual Training and currency training events for Mission Ready Cyberspace Operators and is prepared for events in order to optimize training time available. Monitors assigned military members' go-no-go readiness status and ensures deficiencies are recognized. Works with scheduling section to provide opportunities for assigned members, to maintain full mission readiness. Ensures training for each event has been prepared and is ready. Coordinates with maintenance section to ensure all assigned equipment is in good working condition and ready for each training and mission event.

Spearheading interagency initiatives focused on digital modernization and serving as a principal technical liaison to internal and external stakeholders, including executive leadership and customer agencies to communicate highly technical information, develop cooperative relationships, resolve conflicting priorities, and provide authoritative guidance on AI, software engineering, security, and IT program strategy.

Title: Principal Al Software Engineer | Agency: Technology Transformation Service | Location: Multiple Locations | Grade: GS-15. Qualifications: Integrating security and privacy best practices throughout the digital product development lifecycle, performing technical risk assessments, resolving complex cybersecurity or compliance issues, and advising leadership and stakeholders on security strategy, identity and access management, and regulatory compliance. Leading and mentoring cross-functional teams at scale in highly complex, dynamic and agile environments to include planning, developing, and executing large-scale critical enterprise IT modernization projects, aligning team priorities with organizational objectives, and integrating emergent technologies and industry best practices. US Citizenship or National (Residents of American Samoa and Swains Island) Meet all eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date. Register with Selective Service if you are a male born after 12/31/1959 Serve a one year probationary period, if required.

Title: IT SPECIALIST (INFOSEC) | Agency: Naval Air Systems Command | Location: Point Mugu, California | Grade: DS-4 to 5. Duties: You will serve as an IT Specialist (INFOSEC) for the Point Mugu Sea Range (PMSR) Department, Enterprise Systems Branch as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO). You will assist in developing, maintaining, and updating Assessment and Authorization packages for assigned IT systems and collaborates with other PMSR ISSOs. You will verify that prospective users possess the requisite security clearances, supervisory need-to-know authorizations, and user awareness training before recommending access to DoD Information Systems (IS).

Title: IT SPECIALIST (INFOSEC) | Agency: Naval Air Systems Command | Location: Point Mugu, California | Grade: DS-4 to 5. Qualifications: DS-04: Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-09 grade level or DS-03 pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Risk Management Framework (RMF): Assisting in the preparation, documentation, and review of Assessment and Authorization (A&A) packages across system life cycles; Security Controls & STIGs: Applying and validating Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and Security Requirements Guides (SRGs) on operating systems, network devices, or applications; Vulnerability & Incident Management: Utilizing automated scanning tools (e.g., ACAS/Tenable Nessus) to evaluate vulnerabilities, track POA&Ms (Plan of Action and Milestones), and support incident response; Access & Compliance Monitoring: Performing routine audit log reviews, user access verification, and ensuring adherence to DoD information security instructions and directives. DS-05: Your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or DS-04 pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Title: IT SPECIALIST (INFOSEC) | Agency: Naval Air Systems Command | Location: Point Mugu, California | Grade: DS-4 to 5. Qualifications: Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: A&A Leadership & RMF Lifecycle: Leading, developing, and final-reviewing comprehensive Assessment & Authorization (A&A) packages through all steps of the Risk Management Framework (RMF) to achieve and sustain an Authority to Operate (ATO); Cybersecurity Policy & Governance: Authoring, interpreting, and enforcing DoD-wide and command-level INFOSEC policies, procedures, and system security plans (SSPs); Vulnerability & Risk Mitigation: Directing remediation efforts for complex vulnerabilities, analyzing STIG non-compliance impacts, and managing high-priority Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms); Technical Oversight & Coordination: Providing senior advisory support to the Information System Security Manager (ISSM) and Authorizing Official (AO), while mentoring and guiding junior/journey-level ISSOs and technical teams. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/ https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-a/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Across overseas posts and domestic offices, the following examples illustrate the types of duties and responsibilities typically performed by a DTO: Customer Service Skills: Provide support to users of information management services, including configuring and optimizing software. Train users on new software applications and provide guidance on updated IT policies and procedures. Encourage and facilitate end-user participation in technology and technical decision-making. Information Technology Skills: Administer computer systems and manage system performance, including network setup and system startup, operation, and shutdown. Manage user access: onboard and train personnel, troubleshoot and resolve issues, track and report incidents, support users, and install or replace equipment and components. Operate and maintain both classified and unclassified IT systems including client/server environments, desktops, messaging platforms, web technologies, database and virtual servers supporting LAN/WAN. Oversee telecommunication network services.

Procure IT products and services, test and deploy solutions, and maintain IT inventory and procurement processes. Oversee cloud requirements and support collaboration tools and IT services. Manage pouch operations, the diplomatic post office, and telephone operator programs. Supervise locally employed staff, including system administrators, mailroom personnel, telephone and radio technicians, and switchboard operators. Assign work and manage individual performance. Serve as a member of the embassy or consulate management team and perform additional duties as directed or required by mission needs. Support emergency planning and response, including management of emergency wireless and digital communications.

Title: Senior Enterprise Data Architect, NF5 | Agency: U.S. Marine Corps | Location: Quantico, Virginia | Grade: NF-5. Duties: The Senior Enterprise Data Architect directly supports the Senior Data Scientist and Business Intelligence (BI) Manager by providing technical leadership for the design, modernization, and migration of enterprise data integration platforms supporting federal and public sector programs. As a critical redundancy and continuity layer for Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS), this role establishes the enterprise data model, defines integration strategies, and ensures rigorous data lineage across all organizational systems. The incumbent leads the design and maintenance of the enterprise data model, defining how data entities relate across all MCCS systems. This includes performing foundational schema design and database normalization to support both current environments and future enterprise technology stacks. The role is responsible for maintaining current state and future state architecture artifacts required for compliance, continuity, and system onboarding, while also providing critical architectural coverage for enterprise financial, operational, and customer data systems. The Senior Enterprise Data Architect defines the enterprise data integration architecture, detailing how data moves between source systems, the data lake, and downstream reporting environments.

Title: Senior Enterprise Data Architect, NF5 | Agency: U.S. Marine Corps | Location: Quantico, Virginia | Grade: NF-5. Duties: The role includes architecting, developing, and optimizing complex ETL and ELT pipelines using Oracle Data Integrator (ODI) and Amazon Web Services (AWS) Glue. The incumbent analyzes and modernizes legacy ODI mappings, packages, workflows, and Cognos reports, converting them into cloud native solutions that support modernization efforts. This position is responsible for establishing and documenting enterprise data lineage to ensure full traceability of data origins, transformations, and destinations in accordance with Department of Defense (DoD) compliance requirements, including NIST, FISMA, the Privacy Act, and HIPAA. Additionally, the incumbent defines technical specifications for ETL and ELT pipelines, including transformation logic and data quality rules at the architectural layer. The incumbent serves as the primary technical authority for contractor deliverables and major enterprise data contracts, ensuring all proposed solutions align with MCCS standards and long-term architectural requirements. The role evaluates contractor architectural proposals, validates technical performance, and reviews integration designs to prevent long term technical debt or system failures.

Title: Senior Enterprise Data Architect, NF5 | Agency: U.S. Marine Corps | Location: Quantico, Virginia | Grade: NF-5. Duties: The Senior Enterprise Data Architect partners closely with the Data Governance Supervisor and Contracting Officer to assess technical scope expansions, resolve vendor performance failures, and ensure all contractor provided data solutions meet quality, security, and compliance expectations. This role leads the planning and execution of data migration efforts from on premise and legacy environments to AWS. This includes working directly with external technology providers to map legacy data structures to the new enterprise data model and ensuring that no data assets are lost or orphaned during the transition. The role defines migration strategies, cutover plans, and rollback procedures consistent with federal change management standards and validates data integrity, accuracy, completeness, and performance throughout and after migration activities. The incumbent designs data architectures that comply with federal frameworks and regulatory controls such as FISMA, NIST, and FedRAMP aligned environments. The role implements appropriate data access controls, encryption standards and logging consistent with agency requirements and supports Authority to Operate (ATO) documentation by providing required architectural inputs and technical artifacts. Provides World Class Customer Service with an emphasis on courtesy.

Title: Senior Enterprise Data Architect, NF5 | Agency: U.S. Marine Corps | Location: Quantico, Virginia | Grade: NF-5. Qualifications: Eight or more years of progressively responsible experience in data architecture, data engineering, enterprise data integration, or related technical leadership in a large, complex, or regulated organization. An equivalent combination of relevant education, training, and experience may substitute for a portion of the experience. Experience must demonstrate the ability to analyze and modernize enterprise ETL/ELT workflows, including Oracle Data Integrator (ODI) mappings and packages; design or implement data pipelines with AWS Glue or comparable cloud integration services; and plan or support migration of data from legacy systems to AWS or a comparable cloud environment. Applicants must demonstrate advanced SQL, database normalization, enterprise data modeling, ETL and ELT patterns, data validation and reconciliation, data lineage, operational monitoring, change control, and technical documentation. Working knowledge of relevant AWS services (S3, RDS, Redshift, IAM, and CloudWatch) and analytics platforms such as Snowflake and MicroStrategy is required. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to assess technical designs and contractor deliverables against documented architecture, security, and performance requirements, and communicate findings to stakeholders.

Continuously identifies and analyzes threats and vulnerabilities to the information systems to maintain an appropriate level of protection. Ensures computer software designs address information system security requirements. Accomplishes risk analysis, security testing, and certification due to modifications or changes to computer systems.

Certifies all software prior to installation and use on communications and computer systems. Executes computer security plans and enforces mandatory access control techniques such as trusted routers, bastion hosts, gateways, firewalls, or other methods of information systems protection. 2. Manages the Network Security Program. Maintains required information assurance certification IAW DoD 8570.01-M, Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002, Clinger Cohen Act of 1996. Implements and advises on IT security policies and procedures to ensure protection of information transmitted to the installation, among organizations on the installation, and from the installation using Local Area Networks (LAN), Wide Area Networks (WAN), the World Wide Web, or other communications modes. Controls access to prevent unauthorized persons from using network facilities. Limits access to privileged programs (i.e., operating system, system parameter and configuration files, and databases), utilities, and security-relevant programs/data files to authorized personnel. Implements methods to prevent or minimize direct access, electronic or other forms of eavesdropping, interpreting electro-mechanical emanations, electronic intercept, telemetry interpretation, and other techniques designed to gain unauthorized access to IT information, equipment, or processes. Evaluates unusual circumstances to recognize and define potential vulnerabilities and selects and oversees the installation of physical and technical security barriers to prevent others from improperly obtaining such information. Conducts the Information Assurance Awareness Program which uses computer-based training for both initial and recurring information protection training. Maintains required course records. 3. Serves as the Communications Security (COMSEC) Manager for all cryptographic activities including managing the Cryptographic Access Program (CAP). Formulates and develops communications security criteria and requirements for inclusion in mobility, contingency, and exercise plans.

Leads evaluation, piloting, and deployment of SI, ML, and advanced analytics to enhance regulatory decision-making and streamline scientific processes, consistent with FDA's governance program. Establishes governance frameworks and standards for responsible SI adoption, ensuring alignment with federal policy, ethical guidelines, and FDA strategic priorities. Collaborates with scientific and regulatory program offices to identify opportunities where SI-enabled tools can improve data quality, analytical throughput, and mission outcomes. Conducts strategic IT planning and portfolio management to align technology investments with FDA priorities and modernize data platforms supporting scientific and regulatory needs. Develops and maintains, for approval by the Deputy Commissioner for Technology, a multi-year IT investment roadmap that reflects agency priorities, emerging technology trends, and resource constraints. Oversees the full lifecycle of IT programs and projects, ensuring cost-effective delivery, measurable performance outcomes, and alignment with OMB, HHS, and FDA policies.

Title: Director, Office of Mission Information Technology Services | Agency: Food and Drug Administration | Location: Silver Spring, Maryland. Duties: Advises the Deputy Commissioner for Technology, and senior leadership on technology investment decisions, risk trade-offs, and opportunities to consolidate or modernize legacy systems. Provides enterprise IT services, including application development, infrastructure maintenance, technical support, and cybersecurity to protect sensitive health data. Ensures the availability, reliability, and scalability of IT systems and platforms that support FDA's regulatory, scientific, and administrative functions. Directs the development and maintenance of enterprise applications, data platforms, and shared services that meet the diverse needs of FDA Centers, Offices, and Programs. Establishes and enforces service-level agreements, performance metrics, and customer service standards to ensure responsive and high-quality IT support. Oversees cybersecurity programs and policies to protect sensitive health, regulatory, and administrative data from unauthorized access, breaches, and cyber threats. Ensures compliance with federal cybersecurity requirements including FISMA, NIST frameworks, and HHS/FDA security policies across all IT systems and platforms. Partners with the FDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to assess risk, implement security controls, and respond to cybersecurity incidents. Promotes a culture of cybersecurity awareness and accountability across the IT workforce and among system users agency-wide.

Title: Director, Office of Mission Information Technology Services | Agency: Food and Drug Administration | Location: Silver Spring, Maryland. Duties: Improves operational efficiency and customer service delivery by modernizing legacy systems and establishing a secure, cost-effective IT foundation supporting FDA's regulatory and public health functions. Identifies and prioritizes legacy system modernization opportunities, developing migration strategies that minimize operational disruption and maximize return on investment. Implements cloud computing, automation, and other emerging technologies to reduce technical debt, improve system performance, and lower total cost of ownership. Establishes metrics and reporting mechanisms to track modernization progress and demonstrate value to agency leadership and stakeholders.

Title: Chief Technology Officer | Agency: Small Business Administration | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: Provides executive leadership for the Technology Office, setting its strategic direction, governance, resource priorities, and performance expectations. Develops and carries out a multi-year technology strategy aligned with the agency's mission, customer needs, and legal requirements, and turns business needs into investment and modernization priorities. Directs the Solutions, Architecture, and Engineering Division, setting enterprise standards for solution design, systems engineering, integration, and modernization so that solutions are reliable, secure, and aligned with mission needs. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. Title: Supervisory IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Summary: This position is in the Department of the Chief Information Officer, Information Technology Security Office, Security Operations Division, Security Operations Support Branch. The Division protects the Judiciary from cyber threats, strengthens security and threat awareness, prevents operational disruptions, and provides evaluation services to improve system and program security. Previous applications under announcement #26-CIO-13031720 will be considered.

Title: Supervisory IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: The Supervisory Information Technology Specialist (Security) is in the Information Technology Security Office's Security Operations Division and serves as the Security Operations Support Branch Chief. The Security Operations Branch delivers enterprise detection engineering, threat hunting, threat intelligence, and insider threat capabilities in support of continuous cybersecurity operations. This position reports to the Security Operations Division Chief. The incumbent is a recognized cyber-security subject matter expert with a strong defensive cybersecurity background and is responsible for leading detection engineering, threat hunting, threat intelligence and insider threat teams to identify cybersecurity threats impacting the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of judicial data. The Supervisory Information Technology Specialist (Security) leads hypothesis-based threat hunting to identify, investigate, and mitigate advanced persistent threats, zero-day vulnerability abuse, and other malicious activity to bypass traditional security controls. The incumbent lead detection engineering to categorize known attack vectors through the security information and event management. The incumbent is responsible for the threat intelligence program, reporting on malicious threat actors, and identifying insider threats to judiciary data and systems. Leading, directing, and overseeing the Security Operations Support Branch.

Title: Supervisory IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: Overseeing the development, testing, deployment, and lifecycle management of detection logic used to identify malicious activity. Leading the production and operational integration of threat intelligence to inform detection engineering priorities, hunting hypotheses, and risk-based decision making. Directing proactive threat hunting activities to identify emerging, novel, or evasive adversary behavior not covered by existing detection mechanisms. Establishing and maintaining detection engineering standards, methodologies, and quality assurance processes to support accuracy, consistency, and operational effectiveness. Overseeing the validation, tuning, and refinement of detections based on operational feedback, adversary emulation results, and observed threat activity. Ensuring development of metrics and reporting to measure detection coverage, effectiveness and operational maturity. Leading the development and maintenance of a common operational picture that identifies baseline behavior and meaningful deviations to support shared situational awareness, prioritization and leadership decision making. Providing regular executive summaries to senior leadership and judiciary cybersecurity stakeholders for informed enterprise risk understanding prioritization, and resource allocation decisions. Coordinating closely with Security Operations Center to support alert fidelity, investigative workflows, and continuous improvement of analytic outcomes.

Title: Supervisory IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: Managing branch personnel, contractor support, and resource planning to sustain required capabilities.

Title: IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Summary: This position is in the Department of the Chief Information Technology Officer, Information Technology Security Office (ITSO). ITSO manages the Judiciary's IT security program; protects the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Judiciary information and systems; oversees enterprise security operations and incident response; develops national security policies and guidance; and works with Judiciary and external partners to safeguard IT operations and support the Judiciary's mission.

Title: IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: The IT Specialist (Security) serves as senior level Security Control Assessment subject-matter expert (SME) responsible for leading complex, enterprise-level assessments of security controls across information systems, applications, cloud and hybrid environments. The incumbent provides authoritative technical advice to senior management, Authorizing Officials, and other stakeholders on control effectiveness, security risk, systemic weaknesses, remediation, compensating controls, and residual risk. The selectee will also develop and improve assessment methods, procedures, testing approaches, and quality practices; resolve complex assessment issues; identify systemic and enterprise-wide weaknesses; and provide technical leadership to multidisciplinary assessment teams. The incumbent must also be able to perform the tasks and meet the requirements outlined in NIST Special Publication 800-181 National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education (NICE) Cybersecurity Workforce for the role of Security Control Assessment (OG-WRL-012). Duties Include: Leading complex security control assessments by planning, leading, and conducting enterprise-level assessments of information systems, applications, cloud and hybrid environments; establishing assessment scope, objectives, methodology, evidence requirements, and testing approaches based on system risk and mission impact.

Title: IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: Serving as a senior technical authority and providing independent risk analysis; applying independent professional judgment to evaluate complex technical and security issues and developing risk-based recommendations without assuming risk-acceptance or authorization authority. Developing and improving security control assessment methodologies. Establishing appropriate assessment approaches for complex, emerging, and non-standard technology environments, including cloud, DevSecOps, and other modern architectures. Analyzing systemic and enterprise-level risk and resolve complex assessment issues. Resolving complex or contentious assessment issues involving disputed findings, conflicting evidence, control interpretations, compensating controls, and competing mission requirements and defend assessment conclusions and recommendations before senior technical and management officials. Leading multidisciplinary assessment teams and stakeholder engagement. Providing technical leadership and direction to assessment teams and coordinating assessment activities with system owners, architects, engineers, developers, cybersecurity and privacy personnel, contractors, and other subject-matter experts. Communicating assessment results and support authorization and risk management decisions. Developing clear, accurate, and defensible assessment reports, findings, briefings, and other decision-support materials. Driving continuous improvement of assessment practices.

Title: IT Specialist (Security) | Agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts | Location: Washington, District of Columbia. Duties: Evaluating lessons learned, assessment results, emerging threats, technology changes, and evolving security requirements to identify opportunities to improve assessment quality, efficiency, consistency, and risk-management decision support.

Title: Chief Information Security Officer | Agency: Department of Energy Headquarters | Location: Germantown, Maryland | Grade: GS-14. Evaluate the feasibility, security, and integration of IT hardware, software, networks, and emerging technologies to ensure systems comply with federal standards and mitigate cyber risks. Interpret and enforce federal cybersecurity directives (e.g., FISMA, NIST, OMB, CISA) and monitors organizational adherence to information security, privacy, and supply chain risk requirements. Direct and coordinate cybersecurity incident reporting, investigation, mitigation, response, and recovery efforts across organizational systems and operations. Represent the organization as a leader or member on standing and ad-hoc cybersecurity boards, working groups, and committees to coordinate cross-cutting IT security initiatives.

Evaluating the security risks and feasibility of emerging technologies (such as cloud architectures, automated tools, or advanced communications) and advising executive or senior management on adopting secure technical solutions.

Title: Associate Deputy Chief Information Officer | Agency: Department of Energy Headquarters | Location: Multiple Locations | Grade: GS-15. Duties: The Department of Energy's mission is to ensure America's security and prosperity by addressing its energy, environmental and nuclear challenges through transformative science and technology solutions. The Office of the Chief Information Officer office leads the Department's IT reform initiatives. In an increasingly complex and hostile cyber landscape, the OCIO is fully committed to stewarding DOE information assets by: Leveraging existing information technology and expertise to maximize mission accomplishment and reduce costs Identifying and fostering new and emerging information technology to maximize mission accomplishment and reduce costs Providing Departmental IT governance, policy, and oversight processes to ensure secure, efficient, and cost-effective use of IT resources Ensuring acceptable risk-based cybersecurity by enhancing enterprise situational awareness, developing near real-time risk management, and combating advanced persistent threats Leading the Department's IT reform initiatives is an exciting privilege, and we intend to bring about positive transformation to more effectively support the Department's unique mission. We are truly honored that DOE has been named America's #1 Best Employer for Veterans in 2023 by Forbes-not only among Government agencies, but among employers across the U.S.

Title: Associate Deputy Chief Information Officer | Agency: Department of Energy Headquarters | Location: Multiple Locations | Grade: GS-15. Duties: We are so proud of this ranking which reflects our commitment to the employment of veterans. As so many veterans at DOE renew their service to our Nation, we are deeply committed to their success and advancement. Veterans shape the future of energy As a Associate Deputy Chief Information Officer, you will: Provide executive-level leadership and oversight of an integrated enterprise IT service portfolio, ensuring that customer and mission requirements inform service strategy, design, transition, operations, and continual service improvement. Direct the delivery, availability, reliability, and performance of enterprise IT infrastructure, cloud services, and workplace applications across the Department. Oversee a multi-vendor contract environment of over 300 contractor personnel and directs the financial planning, budget execution, and allocation of approximately $20 million in appropriated funds. Exercise full supervisory authority through subordinate GS-15 leaders over a federal workforce exceeding 25 employees, including setting performance standards, evaluating work, and managing workforce development. Drive the consolidation of commodity IT and the transition to shared services, while directing the secure adoption and scaling of modern platforms, multi-cloud environments, automation, and advanced data capabilities.

Title: Associate Deputy Chief Information Officer | Agency: Department of Energy Headquarters | Location: Multiple Locations | Grade: GS-15. Serve as the principal advisor to the Deputy CIO for EITS, represents the office in high-level Departmental and interagency forums, and exercises delegated managerial decision-making authority in the Deputy CIO's absence.

Title: Computer Systems Administrator | Agency: U.S. Courts | Location: Cleveland, Ohio | Grade: JS-9. Summary: Run the servers. Support the people. Help build the AI tools that support our clients. The Constitution promises everyone a fair trial and equal justice, regardless of race, gender, background, or income. Our office keeps that promise for people who cannot afford a lawyer, and we do it as one team. But behind every motion filed, every witness found, and every trial fought, are colleagues in four offices across northern Ohio-colleagues who count on.

Title: Computer Systems Administrator | Agency: U.S. Courts | Location: Cleveland, Ohio | Grade: JS-9. Duties: Serve as a go-to resource for attorneys and staff, providing responsive help-desk support in person and remotely, and following through until colleagues can work confidently. Set up and run courtroom presentation technology and audiovisual equipment for hearings and trials, so the defense case looks and sounds as strong as it is. Work with legal teams and the Electronic Discovery Coordination Paralegal on discovery, including evidence review platforms, load files, de-duplication, searching, production, and outside vendors. Train staff on applications, security practices, and new tools, and support new employees as they join the office. Travel to our branch offices and provide occasional after-hours support when a deadline or trial requires it. Keep the Office Running Administer Windows servers, Active Directory, Group Policy, Hyper-V, Linux servers, and Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online, Teams, and SharePoint); manage accounts, permissions, patching, and performance. Install, test, and maintain computers, mobile devices, printers, network equipment, and firewalls, along with commercial, Administrative Office (AOUSC), and locally developed software. Diagnose system failures, find the root cause, and fix it, working with external IT staff and vendors as needed.

Title: Computer Systems Administrator | Agency: U.S. Courts | Location: Cleveland, Ohio | Grade: JS-9. Duties: Run and verify backups, including off-site copies; test restores; and maintain disaster recovery and continuity-of-operations plans in line with national judiciary security requirements. Assist with procurement, site surveys, installations, vendor maintenance, and invoice review; document systems and procedures; prepare periodic activity reports; and meet regularly with your supervisor to set priorities. Help Build Our Local AI Tools Help administer the office's on-premises GAI system, including its Linux and GPU hardware, containers, model runtime, user interface, and user access. Improve how discovery is converted into searchable text, using OCR and quality checks, and keep Bates numbers attached to every page so that lawyers can find and verify the exact source. Test the system's accuracy, explain its limits plainly, and teach users to treat AI output as a lead to verify, never as evidence. Keep case data secure and separate by case, evaluate new models and tools, and write scripts that solve real problems for legal teams. Perform other duties as assigned to support the office's mission.

Title: Computer Systems Administrator | Agency: U.S. Courts | Location: Cleveland, Ohio | Grade: JS-9. Qualifications: You must be a high school graduate or equivalent and have a minimum of five years of work experience, including at least two years of progressively responsible experience in systems administration, network support, or IT infrastructure management. Qualifying education may count toward the experience requirement. A bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field from an accredited college or university is preferred. Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to support and train users are essential. Because we have offices across the district, a valid driver's license and good driving record are required. Also: You must have a comprehensive knowledge of systems administration, including continuity-of-operations planning, and strong troubleshooting judgment. You must have an understanding of confidentiality, including the attorney-client privilege, and a willingness to quickly learn about how IT support interacts with criminal law, procedure, and evidence. You must have mature, diplomatic judgment and clear oral and written communication, including the ability to train and support users.

Title: Computer Systems Administrator | Agency: U.S. Courts | Location: Cleveland, Ohio | Grade: JS-9. Qualifications: You must have the ability to lift and move equipment of up to 50 pounds and to travel regularly to our branch offices.

The OIGs were created as independent and objective entities within an agency to (a) promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness in the administration of the agency, and (b) to prevent and detect fraud and abuse in agency programs and operations. The OIGs report to the agency head and Congress through semi-annual and other reports. The GSA OIG operates as an autonomous entity within GSA under a presidentially appointed, Senate confirmed Inspector General who supervises a diverse team of approximately 300 professionals in headquarters' administrative, legal, and operational components and in regional operational offices throughout the country. The GSA OIG is dedicated to protecting the public interest by bringing about positive changes in the performance, accountability, and integrity of GSA programs and operations. Oversight is provided through auditing, inspections and evaluations, and investigations of GSA extensive procurement, real property, and related programs and operations, which primarily support other federal agencies.
